verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission launched from Launch Complex 39B at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "lifted off from Kennedy Space Center’s Launch Complex 39B in Florida at 6:35 p.m. EDT" (R1, URL: /2026/04/01/); "Launch Pad 39B at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida" (R2); "launch of Artemis II from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Pad 39B... Wednesday, April 1" (R3); "liftoff at 6:35 p.m. Wednesday, April 1, 2026... from Kennedy Space Center in Florida" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm the launch location as Launch Complex/Pad 39B at Kennedy Space Center in Florida and the date as April 1, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission lifted off on the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "NASA’s Artemis II SLS (Space Launch System) rocket... lifted off" (R1); "Launching aboard the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state the mission lifted off on the SLS rocket.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission carried four astronauts on a 10-day trip around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, along with CSA... Jeremy Hansen" (four astronauts); "the approximately 10-day Artemis II mission around the Moon" (R1); "four astronauts... on a 10-day mission... orbit the Moon" (R2); "Four astronauts... 10-day mission" (R3, R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly confirm four astronauts and a 10-day mission around the Moon.

verifications.claim: Kennedy Space Center is located in Merritt Island, Florida.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No reference mentions Merritt Island as the location of Kennedy Space Center.

verifications.claim: The specific pad for the Artemis II launch is Launch Pad 39B.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Kennedy Space Center’s Launch Complex 39B" (R1); "Launch Pad 39B at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center" (R2); "Kennedy Space Center's Launch Pad 39B" (R3); "from Kennedy Space Center" with visibility from Launch Pad 39B context (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently identify Launch Pad/Complex 39B as the specific launch pad for Artemis II.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission launch was visible across most of Florida and parts of Georgia.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Nearly all of Florida... and those in southern Georgia, may be able to see Artemis II lift off" (R3); "almost all of the Sunshine State was within range, including parts of Southern Georgia"; "Most of Florida was included in the visibility map" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources provide visibility maps and reports confirming visibility across most of Florida and parts of Georgia.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission marks the first crewed flight of the SLS rocket and Orion spacecraft to the vicinity of the Moon
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "the first crewed flight under NASA’s Artemis campaign" around the Moon (R1); "the first crewed flight of the SLS rocket and Orion spacecraft around the Moon" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly describe Artemis II as the first crewed flight of SLS and Orion to the Moon's vicinity.
